title: Minimally Invasive Surgical Strategies in Intraventricular Tumors: Preliminary Experience with Tubular Retractors for Intraventricular Meningiomas
content:
Intraventricular tumors represent a minority in the context of brain tumors, but their surgical treatment is particularly complex due to their vascularization and visualization, especially in deep localization. The characteristics of these tumors make them ideal candidates for minimally invasive surgical strategies such as the tubular retractor technique, above all in the elderly population.
A 1-year multi-center, retrospective case series was performed: the authors describe their preliminary experience using a neuronavigated tubular retractor in the management of 11 cases of intraventricular meningiomas. Clinical and radiological findings were examined to define the outcome. We used an alternative tubular retractor system obtained by a modified preexisting general surgery trocar or the NICO System BrainPath.
Gross total resection, defined by the removal of all the tumor visible from the brain scans, was achieved in all cases. Ten out of eleven of the patients did not experience major complications or permanent neurological deficits. Four patients presented transitory post-operative agitation, visual blurring and transient hemiparesis. All patients (mean age 72.6 years) were discharged from the hospital in 5-7 days.
Our preliminary experience suggests that the use of navigated tubular retractors is feasible and safe representing a minimally invasive technique by displacing the fibers, hence minimizing the damage of the surrounding cerebral healthy parenchyma. The use of the selective ultrasonic aspirator allows to excise the tumor through the narrow corridor of the tubular lumen of around 2 centimeters and this technique can also be improved using both endoscope and microscope guidance.
